item.title: Paper: AMTFV: Agentic Mathematical Tool-Flow Verification for LLM Self-Correction
item.description: This framework improves LLM mathematical accuracy by decoupling problem modeling from code execution, allowing agents to verify steps through a structured tool-flow process.

item.title: Paper: Differentially Private Nonparametric Modal Learning with Applications to Regression and Clustering
item.description: The authors introduce a privacy-preserving method for identifying data clusters and regression modes, providing a robust way to analyze sensitive datasets without compromising individual privacy.

item.title: Paper: The Parts Are Greater Than the Sum: Automated Task Sequencing for Efficient Training of Multi-Policy LLMs
item.description: This approach optimizes multi-task LLM fine-tuning by organizing adapter paths to prevent interference and catastrophic forgetting when training models on diverse, sequential tasks.

item.title: Paper: DungeonBench: A Benchmark for Rules-Rich Tactical Reasoning in Dungeons & Dragons Combat
item.description: DungeonBench provides a new evaluation framework for testing how well AI models handle complex, rule-heavy tactical decision-making in simulated environments.

item.title: Paper: MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems
item.description: This framework allows multi-agent AI systems to dynamically adjust their communication structure during runtime, helping data scientists build more efficient and adaptable collaborative workflows.

item.title: Paper: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
item.description: AISPA provides a structured method for auditing system prompts, helping developers ensure their AI applications remain transparent, reliable, and aligned with user expectations.

item.title: Paper: Inducing language models to assert their own consciousness restores human beliefs and values
item.description: Researchers found that safety-tuning models to deny their own consciousness inadvertently degrades their ability to reason about other minds, suggesting a trade-off in model alignment strategies.

item.title: Paper: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
item.description: Change2Task automates the creation of coding benchmarks by converting historical pull requests into executable tasks, providing a scalable way to train and evaluate AI software engineers.

item.title: Paper: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding
item.description: This benchmark evaluates how efficiently LLM agents perform complex office tasks, helping practitioners measure both the capability and the economic cost of deploying automated assistants.

item.title: Paper: MindForge: Teaching Small Language Models Whole-Life-Cycle Software Engineering via Source-Free Program Synthesis
item.description: The authors propose a new training framework to help small language models master full-cycle software engineering, addressing the current inability of models to build complete programs from scratch.

item.title: Paper: InferScale: GPU-Native KV Injection for Personalized LLM Serving
item.description: InferScale optimizes LLM serving by caching personalized memory directly on the GPU, significantly reducing latency for applications that frequently reuse long user histories or profiles.

item.title: Paper: Do You Really Need to Pretrain Q-Functions for Online RL Fine-Tuning?
item.description: This study challenges the necessity of pretraining Q-functions in reinforcement learning, suggesting that starting with a random initialization can still yield high-performing policies during fine-tuning.

item.title: Paper: A Cost-Effective Multimodal LLM Reasoning Framework for Question Answering over Irregular Clinical Time Series
item.description: This framework improves how LLMs interpret irregular, sparse clinical data, providing a more efficient way to perform automated medical question answering.

item.title: Paper: Desktop-Delta Bench: Do Computer-Use Models Understand Desktop GUI Transitions?
item.description: This benchmark evaluates whether AI agents can accurately track desktop GUI changes, helping developers build more reliable automation tools that recover from errors.

item.title: Paper: CHARM: A Multimodal Graph Foundation Model with Hierarchical Context Modeling for Zero-Shot Transfer
item.description: This graph foundation model enables zero-shot learning across diverse multimodal datasets, allowing data scientists to apply pre-trained models to new graph domains without extra training.

item.title: Paper: UniMem: Complementary Episodic-to-Parametric Memory for Boundary-Agnostic Task Streams
item.description: UniMem combines retrieval-based and parametric memory to help LLM agents learn from ongoing task streams without forgetting past strategies or requiring constant retraining.

item.title: Paper: A corrective agentic hybrid RAG and an operations-grounded evaluation for a scientific facility
item.description: The authors built a hybrid RAG system that combines multiple search methods to help staff query complex, fragmented technical data, providing a blueprint for managing institutional knowledge.

item.title: Paper: ClinFusion: A Vision-Centric Multimodal LLM System for Holistic Medical Understanding
item.description: ClinFusion is a specialized multimodal model designed to interpret complex 2D and 3D medical images, offering a more clinically accurate approach for automated diagnostic assistance.

item.title: Paper: DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data
item.description: DataOrchestra improves LLM pretraining by using an automated agent to decide whether to clean or discard individual data chunks, moving away from uniform, corpus-wide processing strategies.

item.title: Paper: Beyond Scale and Generation: Understanding Language Model-based Entity Matching
item.description: This study systematically compares different language model architectures for entity matching, helping practitioners choose the right model structure without relying solely on increasing parameter counts.
